Password validator component with real-time requirement feedback

children: Password rules surfaced too late. Users had to submit, discover one failure, correct it, and try again; even the first inline validator revealed only one issue at a time. I reframed validation as continuous guidance so users could see every requirement, understand progress, and recover before submission.

children: What we set out to build
What we set out to build

Create a reusable, accessible validator that explains every requirement as the user types. The component combined a four-step strength meter, live rule checklist, completed-state animation, visibility toggle, and Storybook documentation for reuse across Maui.

I designed the validator as continuous guidance rather than a final gate. The panel appears when typing begins; the strength meter shows overall progress while the checklist identifies the exact rule still blocking completion. I implemented composable rules with debounced updates, keyboard support, screen-reader labels, and contrast-checked colors across desktop and mobile.

Shipped across Signup, Reset, and Settings, then reused by multiple teams through Maui. Showing every requirement before submit replaced the one-error-at-a-time loop with visible progress. Reuse avoided an estimated 6–8 engineering hours per implementation.

attrs.alt: Password validator error and recovery states

children: Real-time feedback works best when users can see both overall progress and the exact rule that still needs attention. Paste events, rapid deletion, keyboard navigation, and screen-reader updates mattered as much as the default typing flow. Adding the component to the design system early made reuse easier across teams.
